FROM ghcr.io/linuxserver-playground/baseimage-selkies:debiantrixie

ENV LSIO_FIRST_PARTY=true

# set version label
ARG BUILD_DATE
ARG VERSION
ARG ORCASLICER_VERSION
LABEL build_version="Linuxserver.io version:- ${VERSION} Build-date:- ${BUILD_DATE}"
LABEL maintainer="thelamer"

# title
ENV TITLE=OrcaSlicer \
    SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt \
    PIXELFLUX_WAYLAND=true

RUN \
  echo "**** add icon ****" && \
  curl -o \
    /usr/share/selkies/www/icon.png \
    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/linuxserver/docker-templates/master/linuxserver.io/img/orcaslicer-logo.png && \
  echo "**** add mozilla apt repo ****" && \
  install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings && \
  curl -o \
    /etc/apt/keyrings/packages.mozilla.org.asc -L \
    https://packages.mozilla.org/apt/repo-signing-key.gpg && \
  echo \
    "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/packages.mozilla.org.asc] https://packages.mozilla.org/apt mozilla main" > \
    /etc/apt/sources.list.d/mozilla.list && \
  printf \
    "Package: *\nPin: origin packages.mozilla.org\nPin-Priority: 1000\n" > \
    /etc/apt/preferences.d/mozilla && \
  echo "**** install packages ****" && \
  apt-get update && \
  DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
  apt-get install --no-install-recommends -y \
    firefox \
    gstreamer1.0-alsa \
    gstreamer1.0-gl \
    gstreamer1.0-gtk3 \
    gstreamer1.0-libav \
    gstreamer1.0-plugins-bad \
    gstreamer1.0-plugins-base \
    gstreamer1.0-plugins-good \
    gstreamer1.0-plugins-ugly \
    gstreamer1.0-pulseaudio \
    gstreamer1.0-qt5 \
    gstreamer1.0-tools \
    gstreamer1.0-x \
    libgstreamer-plugins-bad1.0 \
    libmspack0 \
    libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0 \
    libwx-perl && \
  echo "**** install orcaslicer from appimage ****" && \
  if [ -z ${ORCASLICER_VERSION+x} ]; then \
    ORCASLICER_VERSION=$(curl -sX GET "https://api.github.com/repos/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/releases/latest" \
    | jq -r '.tag_name'); \
  fi && \
  RELEASE_URL="https://api.github.com/repos/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/releases/tags/${ORCASLICER_VERSION}" && \
  DOWNLOAD_URL=$(curl -sX GET "${RELEASE_URL}" | jq -r 'first(.assets[].browser_download_url | select(test("Ubuntu2404_V")))') && \
  cd /tmp && \
  curl -o \
    /tmp/orca.app -L \
    "${DOWNLOAD_URL}" && \
  chmod +x /tmp/orca.app && \
  ./orca.app --appimage-extract && \
  mv squashfs-root /opt/orcaslicer && \
  localedef -i en_GB -f UTF-8 en_GB.UTF-8 && \
  chmod +x /opt/orcaslicer/libexec/orca-slicer-env && \
  sed -i "1a export GDK_BACKEND=x11" /opt/orcaslicer/AppRun && \
  printf "Linuxserver.io version: ${VERSION}\nBuild-date: ${BUILD_DATE}" > /build_version && \
  echo "**** cleanup ****" && \
  apt-get autoclean && \
  rm -rf \
    /config/.cache \
    /config/.launchpadlib \
    /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    /var/tmp/* \
    /tmp/*

# add local files
COPY /root /

# ports and volumes
EXPOSE 3001
VOLUME /config

notes.upstream: # What's Changed This is the OrcaSlicer V2.5.1 release, a maintenance update on top of 2.5.0. Thank you to everyone who reported problems with 2.5.0! It fixes problems connecting and uploading to printers, crashes, slicing bugs and security issues. Toolchangers can now copy per-nozzle settings to every tool, and **Reload from disk** gets a keyboard shortcut. If you chose an HTTPS CA file for a LAN printer before 2.5.1, see **Security** below: you may need to choose it again. ## Downloads | Platform | File | | --- | --- | | Windows installer (x64) | [OrcaSlicer_Linux_AppImage_Ubuntu2404_aarch64_V2.5.1.AppImage](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/releases/download/v2.5.1/OrcaSlicer_Linux_AppImage_Ubuntu2404_aarch64_V2.5.1.AppImage) | | Linux Flatpak (x86_64) | [OrcaSlicer-Linux-flatpak_V2.5.1_x86_64.flatpak](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/releases/download/v2.5.1/OrcaSlicer-Linux-flatpak_V2.5.1_x86_64.flatpak) | | Linux Flatpak (aarch64) | [OrcaSlicer-Linux-flatpak_V2.5.1_aarch64.flatpak](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/releases/download/v2.5.1/OrcaSlicer-Linux-flatpak_V2.5.1_aarch64.flatpak) | | Windows debug symbols (for developers) | [Debug_PDB_V2.5.1_for_developers_only.7z](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/releases/download/v2.5.1/Debug_PDB_V2.5.1_for_developers_only.7z) | # 🌊 New Features & Improvements * **Copy per-nozzle settings to every tool of a toolchanger** by @ianalexis and @raistlin7447 in [17461](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17461) On printers with more than two extruders, such as the Snapmaker U1, the button that copies per-nozzle settings to another extruder was always disabled, so you had to set up each tool by hand. Copying now works for any number of tools, from the process settings, the printer's **Extruder** and **Motion ability** pages, and the material settings. In the process and printer settings, values only go to nozzles of the same volume type, so Standard and High Flow values stay apart. Tools you add by raising the extruder count get their own copy of tool 1's process values, ready to edit. Fixes #16916. The unsaved changes dialog, which the copy goes through, also gets a checkbox for each changed value, so you choose which changes to save, transfer or copy. * **Keyboard shortcut for Reload from disk** by @thelegendtubaguy in [17373](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17373) — **Reload from disk** is bound to Ctrl+Shift+R (Cmd+Shift+R on macOS) in the 3D view and the object list, and you can change the key in the **Keyboard Shortcuts** dialog. The **Clone** and **Reload from disk** items in the right-click menu show the new key right away, without a restart. Fixes #8703. [Wiki](https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/keyboard_shortcuts#customizing-shortcuts) * **The printer connection guide shows the current interface** by @yw4z in [17421](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17421) — the animation in the Device tab that shows how to connect a printer was re-recorded with the current interface. # 🛠️ Bug Fixes ## Security * **AMF files can't freeze OrcaSlicer** by @lamweilun in [17290](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17290) On Windows and macOS, a crafted AMF file with nested XML entities could use up memory and freeze OrcaSlicer, because the XML parser it ships with had its guard against this turned off. The guard is on again, in an updated parser. A file that relies on this kind of expansion no longer imports. Fixes #17287. * **Plugin packages install over a trusted connection** by @HanifKoh in [17292](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17292) — OrcaSlicer installs the Python packages a plugin needs from PyPI with a bundled tool called uv. That tool still trusted a root certificate whose intermediate keys had leaked, so someone between your computer and PyPI who held one of those keys could swap the packages a plugin installs. The bundled uv is updated and no longer trusts that certificate. * **Bambu Lab LAN printers use the HTTPS CA file you choose** by @Alphakilo in [17062](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17062) — the **HTTPS CA File** in the **Connect the printer using IP and access code** dialog had no effect on Bambu Lab printers, so connections that needed it, such as to a self-hosted proxy, failed. OrcaSlicer now saves the CA file with each printer and trusts it when connecting, and the field is no longer greyed out for Bambu Lab printers on Windows and macOS. The file must contain only CA certificates. A CA file chosen before 2.5.1 isn't carried over, so choose it again in the dialog. Fixes #17061. ## Crashes * **No crash when editing an object's speed** by @HanifKoh in [17529](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17529) Since 2.5.0, changing any speed in an object's or part's process settings could close OrcaSlicer with an "out of memory" error. It happened when the process had no extruder variant for the selected printer, for example on a Bowden printer with a process made for direct drive. The settings page now uses the extruder's first variant in that case, as slicing already does. Fixes #17521. * **No crash when clicking in the Measure tool** by @raistlin7447 and @yw4z in [17383](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17383) The **Measure** and **Assemble** tools could crash when you clicked while the cursor was over something they couldn't select, such as an edge highlight off the model, a feature the Assemble tool filters out, or a selection that was just removed. On the Linux Flatpak, it crashed every time. A click like that now acts like a click on empty space. A selected circle's ring also keeps the right thickness as you zoom. Fixes #17367. ## Slicing & Print Quality * **Copies of an object print where they show on the plate** by @Eldenroot in [17183](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17183) — when an object that isn't symmetric had a copy whose first instance was rotated by an angle that isn't a multiple of 90°, that copy could reuse the original's sliced layers. It then printed shifted from where it showed on the plate, with no warning. Such objects are now sliced separately. * **Copies of an object keep their own height ranges** by @Art-Porto in [17279](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17279) — when an object and a pasted copy of it had different height range modifiers, both were sliced the same way. The copy's range was ignored, or the first object's range, such as a filament change, was used on both. Objects whose height ranges differ are now sliced separately. * **Spiral vase works with height range modifiers** by @kisslorand in [17143](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17143) and [17154](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17154) A height range that changed a setting such as wall speed, line width or flow ratio made **Spiral vase** report that the object contains more than one material. An object with a height range modifier was also sliced with several walls instead of one. Spiral vase now checks the filaments assigned to the object, and slices a single wall in every height range. Fixes #8257 and #17022. | Before | After | |--------|-------| | | | * **Height ranges line up with Z shrinkage compensation** by @fa1k3 and @SoftFever in [16491](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/16491) — with **Shrinkage (Z)** set to anything other than 100%, height range modifiers applied their settings at the wrong heights, and a range that reached the top of the object could leave its top layers at the default layer height. Height ranges now follow the compensated height. * **Cleaner multiline infill paths** by @ianalexis in [17341](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17341) — with **Fill Multiline** above 1, Adaptive Cubic, Support Cubic, Honeycomb, Quarter Cubic and Lightning infill could print paths that started in the middle of a line, ran along the walls and ended where they started. Those pieces are joined back together. Single-line infill doesn't change. * **Slicing pipeline plugins run when the preset picks them** by @DIEHARDave in [16884](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/16884) — a plugin chosen in **Slicing Pipeline Plugin** in the process preset could be skipped at slice time with no warning, so the G-code was exported without the plugin's changes. This could happen when the preset's plugin list was built before the plugin finished loading. OrcaSlicer now finds the plugin by name in that case. A plugin that isn't loaded is still skipped. ## Prime Tower & Multi-Material * **The nozzle stays lifted until it's back over the print** by @gazi-faysal-jubayer in [16933](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/16933) Since 2.3.2, after a tool change at the prime tower, the nozzle came down from its lift while it traveled back across the print, which left streaks of color. A lifted nozzle now travels at the lifted height and lowers only at its destination, as it did in 2.3.1. This applies to every lifted travel that ends lower, including detours around walls. Fixes #14968. * **The last filament is unloaded again on single extruder multi-material printers** by @fer-marino and @HanifKoh in [15917](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/15917) and [17496](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17496) Since 2.5.0, on a single extruder multi-material printer, the last filament wasn't rammed and unloaded at the end of the print when the prime tower ended below the top of the print, as it does when a filament is only used on the lower layers. The final unload is written again, at the top layer of the print, so the nozzle doesn't move down into the part. Printers with several tools, including those with multitool ramming such as the Snapmaker U1, are unchanged, so they don't ram in mid-air above the tower. Fixes #15788. * **Prime tower checks apply only when a tower is printed** by @Art-Porto in [16999](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/16999) A plate whose parts all used one filament, with only the **Support/raft interface** on another, was refused before slicing with "The prime tower is only supported if all objects have the same variable layer height", even when no part needed support and no tower would be printed. Such plates are now checked after slicing, and only if a tower is printed. With **No sparse layers (beta)** on, any object taller than the **Height to lid** clearance (Printer settings > Basic information > Extruder Clearance) was refused wherever it stood. An object away from the tower is checked against the real tower height instead. Fixes #16936. | Before | After | |--------|-------| | | | * **Precise Z height no longer makes the prime tower too big** by @HanifKoh in [17204](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17204) — with **Precise Z height** on, a filament change and objects of different heights, slicing could fail with "Prime tower is partially outside the printable area" even though Prepare showed a small tower. The very thin layers where one object ends a few microns above another now print their tower work on the tower layer below. Fixes #17083. * **Gap infill uses the inner wall filament with Classic walls** by @ianalexis in [17229](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17229) — with the Classic **Wall generator**, choosing an outer wall filament in **Filament for Features** also moved the gap infill between walls to that filament. It now prints with the inner wall filament, matching Arachne, which prints inner walls in that space. With a single wall loop, gap infill stays on the outer wall filament. ## Command Line * **The CLI keeps the flushing volumes of multi-nozzle projects** by @HanifKoh in [17440](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17440) — on a printer with more than one nozzle, such as the H2D, a project exported from the command line listed one nozzle volume type for all of its nozzles. When the CLI opened that export again, it recalculated the flushing volumes from the filament colors, so values you had set were lost. The CLI writes one volume type per nozzle instead. A project without volume types takes the printer's default types, as in the GUI, so a printer whose default is High Flow, such as the Prusa CORE One INDX 4T HF and 8T HF, now exports as High Flow. * **No CLI crash when extruder areas don't overlap** by @HanifKoh in [17439](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17439) — a printer profile can give each extruder its own printable area. When those areas only touched or didn't overlap at all, slicing from the command line crashed before placing any object. Objects are now placed on the whole bed in that case, and a prime tower is refused with a message that the extruders share no common area. No bundled printer profile is affected. * **No CLI crash on a mismatched filament order** by @HanifKoh in [17243](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17243) — a plate's custom filament order for other layers is stored as a count and a list of values. When the count didn't match the values, as with `--other-layers-print-sequence-nums 1`, the CLI read past the end of the list and could crash. Such a pair is now treated as no custom order, with a warning in the log. * **No CLI crash on filament presets without a diameter** by @anselor in [16911](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/16911) — since 2.5.0, a CLI run that loaded filament presets without a color crashed when a preset didn't set a diameter, or stopped with a config error when a later filament didn't set the support flag. Missing values now follow the first filament or the option's default. ## Preview * **The preview shows temperature changes on RepRapFirmware** by @ianalexis in [17464](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17464) On printers whose **G-code flavor** is RepRapFirmware, the G-code preview never showed a nozzle temperature change, so a temperature tower looked like it printed at one temperature, and each change was drawn as a retraction. The exported G-code was already right. The preview and its print time estimate now handle these changes correctly. Fixes #14534 and #17436. * **The nozzle marker tilts on belt printers** by @yw4z in [17427](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17427) — in Preview, the nozzle marker stayed upright while the layers were drawn tilted. It now tilts to match the print direction at any belt angle. * **The tool position readout shows the position on its own plate** by @Noisyfox in [17172](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/17172) — on plates after the first, the tool position readout in Preview included the plate's offset in the scene.
